{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the Philippines|Cuisine of the Philippines]]

'''Kare-kare''' is a Philippine stew derived from ''curry'' with a savory peanut sauce.

==Ingredients==
* 1 pack (1.5–2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) oxtail
* 6 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook: Water|water]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Annatto|annatto]] seeds for coloring
* 3 [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplants]]
* 1 lb [[Cookbook:Green Bean|string beans]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Banana Blossom|banana blossom]]
* 1 head [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|cooking oil]]
* 1 cup ground [[Cookbook:Peanut|peanuts]]
* 1 cup toasted ground [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]

==Procedure==
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the oxtail in water until tender.
# Soak annatto seeds in ½ cup water, set aside. Rub the seeds if necessary to bring out color.
# Cut string beans in 3-inch lengths.
# Cut eggplants diagonally, ½-inch thick.
# Cut banana blossoms diagonally, ½-inch thick.
# [[Cookbook:Parboiling|Parboil]] string beans, eggplants and banana blossoms, then set aside.
# [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] garlic and onions in cooking oil.
# Take out the annatto seeds, add the water, and [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] for 5 minutes.
# Stir in ground peanuts and ground rice.
# Bring to a boil, then add the oxtail and vegetables.
# Add more water if needed to have enough sauce; it should be thick and not watery. Add fish sauce to taste.
# Serve with steamed rice and shrimp paste (bagoong) on the side.
